title: Canonical algebraic realization and scalar-unit normalization of pro-etale inverse image
statement:
Let $h:T'\to T$ be any morphism of schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], with compatible small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and the specified inverse images and unit $\eta_h$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, put $RI=h^{-1}R$, and write $I(M)=h^{-1}M$ for the specified inverse-image functor on $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

There is an algebraic inverse-image presentation [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image] whose module functor is exactly $I$ on objects and morphisms and whose underlying sheaf identifications are the canonical ones of the specified inverse image. Define $T(M)=RI\otimes_{RI}I(M)$ and $T(f)=1\otimes I(f)$. The specified functor $T$ therefore has the object and morphism scalar-extension identifications for the identity coefficient map $RI\to RI$.

The multiplication maps $a_M:T(M)\to I(M)$, characterized by $a_M(b\otimes m)=bm$ on local pure tensors, are a natural family of $RI$-module isomorphisms. Their inverses are the scalar insertions $q_M:m\mapsto1\otimes m$; in particular $a_Mq_M=1$ and $q_Ma_M=1$ as sheaf maps.

For any normalized CanonicalRingedTensorComparison $(q,\mu)$ for this specified $T$, the identity coefficient map and the above algebraic presentation [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison], put
$$b_{M,N}=(a_M\otimes a_N)\circ\mu_{M,N}\circ a_{M\otimes_RN}^{-1}.$$
For every object $V$ of $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$, $s\in M(V)$ and $t\in N(V)$, let $h^{-1}s$ denote the unit image in $I(M)(T'\times_TV)$, and similarly for $t$ and $s\otimes t$. Then
$$b_{M,N}\bigl(h^{-1}(s\otimes t)\bigr)=h^{-1}s\otimes h^{-1}t.$$
Here each pure tensor is its image under the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map.

proof.text: Write $L$ for the specified set-sheaf inverse image. By [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor], applied to the base-change functor and compatible small sites specified in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], $L$ preserves finite limits. Denote its binary-product comparison by $\lambda_{X,Y}:L(X\times Y)\xrightarrow{\sim}LX\times LY$. The specified ring and module inverse images in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] use exactly the transported operations: for example the action on $I(M)$, through the canonical underlying-sheaf identifications, is $L(\operatorname{act}_M)\circ\lambda_{|R|,|M|}^{-1}$; addition uses the same formula, and zero and one use the final-object comparison. Take these canonical identifications as $e_R,e_M$ of [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image], and take its module functor to be $I$ itself. To verify the graph conditions, an equation $z=\operatorname{act}_M\circ\langle x,y\rangle$ gives $Lz=L(\operatorname{act}_M)\circ\lambda^{-1}\circ\langle Lx,Ly\rangle$, since the two sides of $\lambda\circ L\langle x,y\rangle=\langle Lx,Ly\rangle$ have identical projections. The same argument treats addition and multiplication; the final-object comparison treats zero and one. These are precisely the required graph equations. On morphisms the specified inverse image uses the underlying $Lf$, so $e_M$ is natural and the resulting presentation has exactly $I$ on both objects and arrows.

source.place: Tag 03D2, lemma-pullback-module; sites.tex Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi; expanded matching of the specified transported operations

proof.text: For an $RI$-module sheaf $H$, sectionwise scalar multiplication $(b,m)\mapsto bm$ is $RI$-bilinear: distributivity gives additivity in each argument and commutativity of $RI$ gives $(cb)m=c(bm)=b(cm)$. It commutes with every restriction. Thus [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] gives a unique module-sheaf map $a_H:RI\otimes_{RI}H\to H$ with $a_H(b\otimes m)=bm$. The insertion $q_H:H\to RI\otimes_{RI}H$, $m\mapsto1\otimes m$, is a sheaf map by restriction compatibility and the presheaf-to-sheaf tensor map of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. It is additive, and is $RI$-linear because $1\otimes cm=c\otimes m=c(1\otimes m)$, the balanced tensor relation. These computations take place in the sectionwise presheaf tensor and therefore hold after its map to the sheaf tensor.

source.place: Section 03EK, section-tensor-product, tensor definition and displayed Hom--Bilin universal property; explicit identity-scalar formulas

proof.text: For every local section $m$ of $H$, $a_Hq_H(m)=1m=m$. The maps $q_Ha_H$ and $1$ from $RI\otimes_{RI}H$ to itself agree after the pure-tensor pairing, since $q_Ha_H(b\otimes m)=1\otimes bm=b\otimes m$. The injectivity in [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] makes them equal as sheaf morphisms. Consequently $a_H$ and $q_H$ are inverse $RI$-module-sheaf isomorphisms. This proves equality on the entire sheafified tensor, without assuming that every section is a global sum of pure tensors.

source.place: Section 03EK, displayed Hom--Bilin universal property; cancellation of multiplication and insertion

proof.text: For a module-sheaf map $v:H\to H'$, $v(bm)=bv(m)$, so $v\circ a_H$ and $a_{H'}\circ(1\otimes v)$ agree on the pure-tensor pairing and hence everywhere by [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal]. Also $(1\otimes v)q_H(m)=1\otimes v(m)=q_{H'}v(m)$. Apply this to $H=I(M)$ and $v=I(f)$. The assignments $T(M)=RI\otimes_{RI}I(M)$, $T(f)=1\otimes I(f)$ obey identity and composition laws: the two maps in each law agree on $b\otimes m$ and thus everywhere by the same injectivity. They are exactly extension of scalars for $1_{RI}$, on objects and morphisms, by the sheaf tensor definition [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The maps $a_M:=a_{I(M)}$ and $q_M:=q_{I(M)}$ are the asserted natural inverse families.

source.place: Section 03EK, section-tensor-product and Hom--Bilin universal property; naturality on scalar tensors

proof.text: Let $(\widetilde q,\mu)$ be any comparison in [def-weil-pbc-canonical-ringed-tensor-comparison] for this $T$ and the presentation of step 1. Its q_one condition says $\widetilde q_H=q_H$ on every section. Put $Z=|M|\times|N|$, let $x,y$ be its projections, and let $z:Z\to|M\otimes_RN|$ be the canonical pure-tensor pairing [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $s\in M(V)$ and $t\in N(V)$, apply the comparison's generalized pure-tensor equation to the section $\eta_{h,Z,V}(s,t)$ of $(LZ)(T'\times_TV)$. Naturality of the specified unit [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] for $x,y,z$ identifies its images with $h^{-1}s$, $h^{-1}t$, and $h^{-1}(s\otimes t)$, respectively, under the canonical identifications of step 1. Hence $\mu_{M,N}q_{M\otimes_RN}(h^{-1}(s\otimes t))=q_M(h^{-1}s)\otimes q_N(h^{-1}t)$. Step 3 identifies $q_{M\otimes_RN}$ with $a_{M\otimes_RN}^{-1}$. Applying $a_M\otimes a_N$ to this equality and using $a_Mq_M=a_Nq_N=1$ yields exactly $b_{M,N}(h^{-1}(s\otimes t))=h^{-1}s\otimes h^{-1}t$. All pure tensors here are followed by the presheaf-to-sheaf map. The argument uses a product test sheaf, so needs no representability assumption or unstated rule about inverse images of represented sections.
